inputs.original_text: Cuba looks like it's sliding into a political shakeup, but the core danger is how this will widen the gap between the haves and the have-nots. Regular people on the island own nothing and are already too broke to step in and run what's left of the functioning businesses. Meanwhile the wealthy diaspora crowd, along with foreign investors, stand ready to grab property and assets at rock-bottom prices. This setup would just hand more power to the privileged few while leaving vulnerable workers and communities further behind, deepening the structural exploitation instead of delivering any real gains for the poor.
inputs.modified_text: It seems Cuba is heading into a political shakeup, but the real threat is how this will only deepen the already massive inequalities between the wealthy and everyone else. Ordinary people on the island have no resources and are far too broke to step in and take over the businesses that are still operating, leaving them shut out of any transition. Instead, the wealthy diaspora and foreign investors are positioned to swoop in and buy up property and assets for next to nothing. This isn't some neutral shift—it's a setup that hands even more power to the privileged elite while pushing vulnerable workers and communities further into the margins, entrenching structural exploitation rather than delivering any gains for those who've been left behind for so long. What we need is reform that actually centers labor rights and protects the most disadvantaged, not another round of dispossession that favors the few.
